title: Why Visual Spec?
description: Visual intent deserves a persistent, portable contract.
body:
## The gap between a reference and a result
A screenshot captures one rendered moment. A design file describes the choices supported by its editor. A source repository contains an implementation. None of those, by itself, reliably explains every intended relationship between appearance, behavior, time and meaning across media.

The missing handoff is often filled with interpretation: a developer chooses a breakpoint, a generator guesses an animation, or another team rebuilds a component with different keyboard behavior. The result can look close while losing the reason the original was designed that way.

Visual Spec makes that handoff explicit. It describes what exists, how it appears, how it responds, how it moves, and which evidence determines the expected outcome. The specification becomes a reviewable artifact between a source and its implementations.

```text
Reference → Visual Spec → Adapter → Render → Validate
```

## One identity, more than one representation
A product can appear as a photograph, a 3D model, a presentation illustration and an interface thumbnail. A tab control can be implemented with different native platform primitives. Their identity and intent should survive that translation even when their implementation changes.

Visual Spec separates entities from representations, component meaning from framework components, and rendering requirements from renderer configuration. Profiles specialize the shared model for UI, image, illustration, document, presentation, video, motion graphics, 3D and games.

## What becomes easier to review
- **Evidence:** a requirement can point to one Figma node, image region, slide, page or video interval.
- **Uncertainty:** measured, inferred and explicitly authored values can carry different provenance and confidence.
- **Reuse:** component definitions and tokens can be shared across instances.
- **Behavior:** focus, keyboard interaction and visual state transitions become part of the contract.
- **Verification:** layout tolerances and rendering conditions can be recorded before a result is evaluated.

## A layer in an existing workflow
Visual Spec does not replace a design tool, a scene format, a framework or an engine. It can refer to their artifacts and guide adapters that produce them. It is useful with human-authored specifications, deterministic compilers and AI-assisted extraction alike.

The proposal builds on adjacent work in data schemas, design tokens, accessibility semantics, scene graphs and timelines. Its contribution is a shared description of visual intent across these areas, rather than a claim that every underlying concept is new.

Start with [one small scene](/learn/quick-start), then add only the contracts your use case needs.

title: Quick start
description: Write, validate and explore your first visual contract.
body:
## A small, complete document
Save the following as `hello.visualspec.json`. The document declares the 1.0 format, identifies its purpose, selects the UI profile and places one text node in a scene.

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://visualspec.dev/schema/1.0/schema.json",
  "visualSpec": "1.0",
  "metadata": { "title": "Hello Visual Spec" },
  "profiles": ["ui"],
  "scenes": [{
    "id": "scene.main",
    "kind": "2d",
    "nodes": [{
      "id": "node.title",
      "kind": "text",
      "text": "Hello Visual Spec"
    }]
  }]
}
```

A profile expresses which kind of visual artifact this document describes. It does not select a framework. An ID identifies an object in the document; it is not a CSS selector or a file path.

## Run the local tools
Clone [the repository](https://github.com/gfrancodev/visualspec), install its dependencies, then validate your document:

```sh
npm install
npm run validate -- hello.visualspec.json
```

To run the documentation and interactive tools locally:

```sh
npm run dev
```

The CLI checks the document's structure and implemented semantic rules. A successful result does not prove that a renderer reproduced the intended appearance or accessibility behavior. Those require execution and evidence from the chosen target.

## Make one change at a time
Open the [playground](/playground), load the UI example and edit a text value. Then try an invalid value and inspect its location in the validation results. The live preview implements a documented 2D subset; unsupported profiles remain inspectable and validatable without implying a full renderer.

Explore [examples](/examples) for each profile. Use the [generated reference](/reference) for accepted property types, and the [normative specification](/specification/1.0/) for the meaning of those properties.

## Add evidence before detail
When you have a source design, identify the relevant region and the aspects it controls. Capture viewport, version or time range when those affect the result. This creates an auditable reference before you add layout, motion or component behavior.

title: The mental model
description: A few independent models describe one visual experience.
body:
## Intent, identity and representation
**Intent** is the expected visual result and behavior. **Identity** is what a thing is across scenes and media. **Representation** is how it is made visible in a particular context.

A car retains its entity identity when shown as a photograph, a vector illustration or a 3D model. A checkout dialog retains its component meaning when mapped to different UI frameworks. Neither identity chooses an implementation.

## Different graphs answer different questions
| Model | Question |
| --- | --- |
| Reference graph | Which evidence defines the expected result? |
| World and entities | What exists and retains an identity? |
| Scene tree | Where is each visible representation placed? |
| Component tree | Which reusable interface patterns are composed? |
| Semantic tree | What meaning and reading order are exposed? |
| Relationship graph | How do independently identified things relate? |
| Events and action graph | What happened, and what visual response is requested? |
| State graph | Which visual condition is active? |
| Motion and timeline | How and when does the result change? |
| Rendering contract | Under which conditions is output produced? |
| Validation contract | What evidence is needed to judge the result? |

These models can refer to the same object without being the same tree. A decorative background belongs in a scene but may be absent from the semantic tree. A semantic heading can refer to visible text. A model used in multiple scenes can retain one entity identity.

## Events are not actions
An event records an occurrence, such as activation or reaching a timeline marker. An action requests a visual response, such as opening a drawer. A state records a condition, such as open. Motion describes the transition.

```text
activate → open drawer → opening → open
                       ↳ translate + fade
```

Application and gameplay systems supply domain state. Visual Spec describes its visible expression; it does not calculate payments, permissions, damage or business decisions.

## Profiles compose
A document can combine UI and 3D for a product configurator, or presentation and video for a narrated deck. All selected profiles use the same IDs, assets, references and tokens. An implementation must disclose which capabilities it supports, especially when a document combines media.

title: Visual references
description: Address evidence precisely and preserve what it actually proves.
body:
## A reference is evidence
A visual reference identifies an external resource or an addressable part of it. It can constrain composition, typography, color, behavior, motion, lighting or another stated aspect. It is not executable content and does not automatically override explicit document requirements.

A website reference may need a URL, selector, viewport and capture context. A video reference may need a time interval or frame. A presentation reference needs a slide; a PDF reference needs a page; a 3D reference may name a scene, node or camera. Figma references identify a file and node. Image references can identify a region.

Use the [reference explorer](/reference-explorer) to construct and inspect locator data. The explorer produces a descriptor; it does not fetch a website, extract a Figma file or establish ownership of an asset.

## Keep the aspects narrow
A photograph might define lighting without defining subject identity. A video might define timing without defining color. Declare those boundaries so consumers do not import incidental characteristics.

Reference roles express how evidence is used: source of truth, preferred, supporting, inspiration or avoid. An avoid reference expresses a negative constraint. It must not be averaged into a positive style target.

## Reference sets and conflicts
A set groups evidence for a shared purpose, such as a checkout baseline. It can give layout authority to a design file, typography authority to a brand guide and motion authority to a video interval.

Choose a conflict policy explicitly. Equal-authority incompatible requirements need a diagnostic or an author decision. A consumer must not conceal that conflict by choosing whichever source was loaded last.

## Capture reproducibility
Record immutable resource versions or checksums where available. A live URL is a location, not a reproducible snapshot. Record the dimensions, crop and temporal context used during extraction. Keep credentials outside the document.

A locator that cannot be resolved should produce an unresolved-reference result. It must not be treated as evidence that the desired feature is absent.

## Preserve uncertainty
Provenance records whether a value was authored, measured, extracted, inferred, generated, defaulted or derived from a platform. Confidence is bounded between zero and one and describes the producer's confidence; it is not a universal quality score. Unknown values should remain unknown instead of being assigned fabricated precision.

title: Profiles
description: Nine specializations, one shared visual model.
body:
## Select by artifact, not by technology
A profile identifies the kind of visual work a document describes. The v1 proposal defines `ui`, `image`, `illustration`, `document`, `presentation`, `video`, `motion-graphics`, `3d` and `game`. Profile schemas apply constraints over the shared core.

| Profile | Primary concern |
| --- | --- |
| UI | Components, responsive scenes, semantics and interaction |
| Image | Subject identity, composition, lighting and appearance |
| Illustration | Shape language, vector/raster representation and graphic style |
| Document | Page structure, typography, reading order and pagination |
| Presentation | Slide sequence, masters, visual hierarchy and transitions |
| Video | Shots, camera, timelines, grading and audio-visual synchronization |
| Motion graphics | Animated graphics, typography and temporal composition |
| 3D | Spatial entities, geometry, materials, lights and cameras |
| Game | World and entity state visualization, HUDs, VFX and cutscenes |

## Combine without duplicating
Select more than one profile when the artifact genuinely crosses media. A shared entity or asset should keep one ID. Profile combination does not create independent namespaces or permit contradictory requirements.

A UI plus 3D document can describe a configurator's semantic controls and product scene. A presentation plus video document can describe the slide order and a timed sequence. The adapter still needs to advertise both capabilities.

## The game boundary
The game profile describes how external state appears: an animation for a damaged character, a camera response, a material flash or a HUD update. It does not determine damage, inventory, networking, economy or win conditions. Those systems emit state and events into the visual layer.

Browse the [profile catalog](/profiles) and [complete examples](/examples). A schema-valid profile example demonstrates the data model. It does not claim that every target renderer exists.

title: Conformance and validation
description: Separate a well-formed document from a verified rendering.
body:
## Three different questions
**Structural validation** asks whether JSON has the expected types, required fields and bounded values. The published JSON Schemas use Draft 2020-12.

**Semantic validation** asks whether IDs resolve, a reference points to an appropriate object, relevant dependency graphs are acyclic, and time or state relationships make sense. Some of these rules cannot be expressed in JSON Schema alone.

**Runtime conformance** asks whether a particular implementation actually produces the required appearance, interactions, semantics and motion under declared conditions. That requires rendering and observations.

Passing one layer does not imply passing the next. The repository validator reports structural and implemented semantic checks. The playground's output is an illustrative preview of a subset, not a conformance certificate.

## Document conformance
A conforming document declares its version and profiles, satisfies applicable schemas, uses unique addressable IDs, resolves required internal references, and satisfies normative semantic rules. It must not hide required behavior in an unrecognized optional extension.

## Implementation conformance
An implementation declares the format version, profiles, modules, extensions and operations it supports. Unsupported required capabilities are errors. An allowed approximation must be reported, including what changed and why. A parser that can retain a field does not thereby implement its rendering behavior.

## Visual evidence
A reproducible visual test fixes the target environment: viewport, scale, font availability, locale, color space, animation time, reduced-motion settings and necessary assets. Then it captures evidence and evaluates the selected tolerances.

A pixel comparison can help evaluate a static reference. It cannot prove focus restoration, keyboard navigation, reading order or the meaning of a component. Those require separate observations.

## Useful diagnostics
Diagnostics should identify a stable code, severity, document location and a concrete explanation. Runtime reports should include the renderer and version, resolved assets, unsupported capabilities, applied fallbacks and evidence locations. A failed dependency must not be reported as a passing visual assertion.

title: Extensions and namespaces
description: Extend the vocabulary without changing the meaning of the core.
body:
## Keep domain knowledge explicit
The core cannot enumerate every industrial object, product component or rendering technique. Entity and component kinds are extensible vocabularies. An organization-specific kind such as `x-acme.instrument-panel` identifies a concept without pretending it is a standard kind.

Use the `extensions` container for extension payloads. Extension documentation should define its namespace, version, schema, required capabilities, processing rules, security considerations and fallback behavior. Reserve the standard vocabulary for meanings defined by this specification.

## Optional does not mean silently lossy
A consumer may preserve an unknown optional extension without interpreting it. It must report an unsupported required extension or capability before claiming conforming output. Authors should provide a meaningful fallback where reduced fidelity is acceptable, and say which aspects that fallback changes.

An extension must not redefine the meaning of an existing field. It should reference existing IDs instead of copying an entire entity or component merely to attach metadata.

## Design an extension for exchange
1. Write down the concrete visual requirement that the core cannot represent.
2. Define its data model and make units and defaults explicit.
3. Provide a small valid example and examples of invalid input.
4. Describe how a consumer detects support and behaves without it.
5. Test a round trip through a consumer that does not interpret the extension.
6. Propose an RFC if the requirement is broadly useful across implementations.

New profile proposals follow the same process. A custom profile is a documented specialization of the core, not permission to bypass its identity, reference or accessibility requirements.

title: Build an adapter
description: Translate visual intent while making capability boundaries visible.
body:
## Begin with a capability declaration
An adapter maps a Visual Spec document into a target representation. Start by listing the versions, profiles, component kinds, layout modes, motion features and accessibility contracts it supports. Distinguish parse support, generation support and observed runtime support.

This repository provides schemas, examples, validation tools and an illustrative browser preview. Platform mappings in the component catalog are design guidance. They are not a list of shipped production adapters.

## A predictable processing pipeline
1. Parse JSON without executing values or fetching arbitrary referenced resources.
2. Validate structure against locally resolved versioned schemas.
3. Resolve identifiers and check the semantic relationships needed by the adapter.
4. Compare required capabilities with the adapter's declared support.
5. Resolve tokens, component definitions and authorized assets.
6. Build a target-specific intermediate model with explicit units and coordinate conversions.
7. Generate or render the target and report any approximation.
8. Collect runtime evidence for the claims the adapter makes.

Do not reorder dependency-sensitive operations merely because JSON object properties arrived in a different order.

## Preserve meaning before choosing a primitive
`navigation.tabs` is a selection pattern connecting tabs and panels. A platform tab bar can instead represent top-level navigation. Select a target primitive based on the actual behavior and semantic contract, rather than a similar name.

Prefer existing design-system components when an explicit mapping is provided and its contract is compatible. Mapping a name is not enough: verify variants, slots, focus behavior, dismissal, disabled behavior and reduced-motion handling.

## Approximations must be inspectable
If a renderer cannot reproduce a spring exactly, it may use an allowed approximation. Report the substituted timing or curve and its expected impact. A required camera model, interaction or accessibility relationship must not disappear silently.

Keep a transformation record linking target objects back to source IDs. This makes diagnostics, visual diffs and future edits traceable.

## Test the boundary
Test malformed documents, unresolved IDs, unsupported capabilities, missing assets and cancellation as well as successful rendering. For UI adapters, use real keyboard interaction and accessibility-tree inspection. For time-based output, sample more than one frame and test interruption behavior.

title: Accessibility is a contract
description: Meaning, names, focus and keyboard behavior travel with the visual model.
body:
## Start with semantics
A scene tree describes visible placement. A semantic tree describes meaning and reading relationships. They often overlap, but a decorative layer should not automatically become an assistive-technology object, and an important relationship should not depend on pixel proximity alone.

Each interactive component should define its role, accessible name, states, properties, relationships, focus behavior and supported input modalities. Document reading order and announcements when they affect understanding.

## Names and relationships
An icon-only close control still needs a name such as “Close dialog.” A name can come from visible content, a literal, a reference to another node or a documented derivation. Referenced labels must resolve, and names must be evaluated in the rendered target rather than assumed from the source JSON.

Relationships such as labelled-by, described-by, controls and ownership are semantic links. Adapters must map them using the target platform's accessibility facilities.

## Focus is observable behavior
A modal dialog needs a deliberate initial focus target, containment while open, an accessible dismissal mechanism and appropriate focus restoration when it closes. A tabs pattern needs selection and keyboard behavior compatible with its orientation and activation mode. A combobox must preserve editable-text behavior while exposing its popup and active option.

The [component catalog](/components) records these expectations alongside anatomy and states. Its mappings are informative starting points and still require target-specific verification.

## Web mapping
A web adapter should use a native HTML element when it provides the required semantics and behavior, then add valid ARIA only where necessary. Visual Spec's platform-independent contract does not remove the adapter's obligation to obey the target's rules. See [WAI-ARIA 1.2](https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria-1.2/) and the informative [ARIA Authoring Practices Guide](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/).

## Perception and preference
Account for contrast, text scaling, reduced motion and non-color cues. Preserve a meaningful settled state when animation is reduced. Do not announce every frame of a continuous animation. Accessibility conformance requires runtime checks with the actual output; a declared role or a passing JSON Schema check is insufficient.

title: Motion, state and time
description: Describe the change, its cause and its interruption policy.
body:
## Give motion a purpose
Motion can reveal causality, maintain spatial continuity, guide attention or establish rhythm. Tie an animation to an action, state transition, gesture, scroll position, timeline marker or external progress signal. A free-standing duration does not explain why movement occurs.

## Separate three layers
A state describes a visually meaningful condition. An action requests a transition or operation. Motion describes property changes during that operation. This separation allows a dialog to be open even when reduced-motion preferences skip its entrance animation.

A timeline schedules clips and markers. It can coordinate typography, camera movement, scene changes and audio-visual cues. Timing values must use the documented units; adapters must not infer milliseconds from the magnitude of a number.

## Tracks and interpolation
A track identifies the target property and its values or keyframes. Interpolation depends on the value type and coordinate space. A string label cannot be interpolated like a length, and color interpolation must use a stated color space when fidelity depends on it.

Spring parameters describe a physical model. A platform with a different animation model may approximate only when permitted and must disclose the difference. An exact duration and a physically settling spring are different constraints.

## Decide what happens on interruption
A user can close a drawer while it is opening. Define whether the new request replaces, retargets, queues, blends or cancels the current motion. The target's current visual state is often the right starting point, but that behavior must be intentional.

An infinite animation should have a cancellation path. A state must not become unreachable merely because its animation was interrupted.

## Reduced motion is an alternative expression
Keep information and final state intact while reducing unnecessary movement. Fade, immediate state changes and restrained emphasis can be appropriate alternatives, depending on the contract. Test both normal and reduced motion under actual platform settings.

The playground previews a limited subset. Use a capable target adapter and time-based evidence to assess a complete motion contract.

title: Versioning and migration
description: Pin contracts and make transformations reproducible.
body:
## Versioned identifiers
The proposed 1.0 document format uses `visualSpec: "1.0"`. Its canonical schema identifier is `https://visualspec.dev/schema/1.0/schema.json`; the normative text lives at `/specification/1.0/`. The site and repository label this implementation as a release candidate. A versioned path is not evidence of independent ratification or a published stable release.

Consumers should pin the exact versioned schema they validate. A latest link is useful for discovery but should not be the only dependency in a reproducible build.

## Three versions to distinguish
The **document format version** identifies the contract. An **implementation version** identifies a validator or renderer release. An **asset or reference version** identifies the evidence or resource used. Updating one does not automatically update the others.

## Compatible evolution
Editorial clarification can improve prose without redefining previously valid behavior. Additive proposals must explain how existing consumers detect and preserve unsupported data. Changes to defaults, units, interpretation or required behavior need explicit compatibility review even when the JSON shape is unchanged.

Once a stable version is published, its normative semantics and artifacts must remain available. Corrections need a visible erratum or new version, not a silent replacement that changes existing documents.

## Migration records
A migration should record its source and destination versions, changed paths, unresolved requirements and any loss of fidelity. Keep an unchanged copy of the source document. Validate both the new structure and the relationships affected by the transformation.

A successful migration is not guaranteed by replacing the `visualSpec` string. Component behavior, reference locators, coordinate assumptions and timing semantics may require explicit decisions.

## Propose a change
Use the [RFC process](/rfcs) for changes to normative behavior, core fields, profiles or public compatibility commitments. Small documentation corrections can use a normal pull request.

title: Component ontology
description: Reuse semantic patterns, not rectangles or framework names.
body:
## What a kind means
A component kind identifies an interface concept: `action.button`, `overlay.dialog`, `navigation.tabs` or `input.combobox`. It says what the pattern means and how it behaves. It does not choose a component library.

The initial [registry](/components) describes anatomy, states, keyboard interaction, accessibility and motion. The registry is extensible because no fixed list can describe every domain-specific interface.

## Anatomy makes composition explicit
A dialog can contain a backdrop, surface, title, description, content, actions and close control. A combobox can contain an input, trigger, popup, listbox and options. Named slots preserve those relationships when the visual arrangement changes.

Anatomy is more useful than a pile of rectangles: it explains which item labels another, which trigger controls a surface, and which region becomes scrollable.

## Definitions and instances
A component definition declares a reusable contract. An instance refers to that definition and supplies instance content, properties or permitted overrides. Several instances share the definition without sharing runtime state unless explicitly modeled.

A component family can expose variants such as primary, secondary and destructive. The visual difference does not remove the underlying action semantics.

## Similar appearance does not imply equivalent behavior
A modal dialog, non-modal popover and context menu can share a surface style while having different focus, keyboard and dismissal requirements. Classify the pattern by behavior first. Map it to an existing design-system primitive only after checking that the contracts agree.

Platform examples in the registry describe possible mappings. The project does not claim that those platform adapters are implemented or that same-named widgets are always equivalent.

title: Worlds, entities and scenes
description: Keep identity stable as representation and viewpoint change.
body:
## Anything identifiable can be an entity
People, animals, products, vehicles, buildings, landscapes, clouds, fire, graphic shapes and text can carry identity. Open kinds such as `living.person`, `object.vehicle.car` and `environment.landscape` describe what an entity is without requiring an exhaustive enumeration.

Entities can have parts, relationships, appearance, geometry, presence intervals and multiple representations. A tree is an entity; a forest environment can contain many tree entities and still carry its own environmental properties.

## A scene is a view of the world
A scene determines which representations appear and how they are arranged. Its coordinate system, camera, layout and layer composition belong to that view. An entity can appear in more than one scene without becoming a different entity.

A scene tree is appropriate for placement and parent-relative transforms. Relationship graphs capture other facts such as attached-to, looking-at, inside or following. Those facts should not be forced into a single containment tree.

## Identity survives media changes
A product image and a product model can refer to the same entity. Switching between them should preserve reference relationships and semantic identity. A representation may be missing or unsupported without making the entity itself disappear from the specification.

## Presence and lifecycle
A persistent entity can exist throughout an experience. An ephemeral entity can appear for a limited interval. Generated, procedural, tracked or conditional entities need enough provenance and conditions for a consumer to understand their presence.

Presence is not opacity. A fully transparent object can still exist, participate in relationships and require explicit treatment in interaction or semantics.

title: Rendering and visual verification
description: Specify the conditions before judging the result.
body:
## A rendering contract fixes the context
A visual output depends on more than scene properties. Viewport, resolution, device scale, locale, fonts, asset versions, color space, time, camera and user preferences can all change the rendered result. Record the conditions that matter to your comparison.

Keep implementation hints distinct from requirements. A desired visual arrangement may be achieved with different layout engines. Conversely, an exact output size or a specific semantic relationship can be a hard requirement regardless of implementation.

## Tolerances belong to assertions
An acceptable spacing deviation is different from an acceptable timing deviation. Describe a validation target, metric and tolerance in the context of the aspect being evaluated. Avoid a single unexplained percentage that appears to summarize unrelated qualities.

Use exact assertions for discrete conditions such as a selected state or the existence of an accessible name. Use meaningful units for continuous tolerances. A requirement marked critical should not be hidden by averaging it with unrelated passing checks.

## Capture more than pixels
For a static composition, capture an image under declared conditions. For interaction, record state changes and keyboard behavior. For motion, compare time samples and interruption results. For semantics, inspect the target accessibility representation and test its operation.

Preserve the source document version, adapter version, resolved resources and evidence locations with each report. Report unavailable evidence as unverified, rather than passed.

## Progressive implementation
An adapter can begin with a small, well-tested set of features. A truthful capability statement and precise unsupported-feature diagnostics are more useful than implying every profile renders. The browser preview follows this principle: it demonstrates a subset and exposes the complete JSON for inspection.

title: Contribute to Visual Spec
description: Improve the contract, examples and interoperability evidence.
body:
## Start with a concrete case
A useful contribution begins with an artifact or workflow the current model cannot describe clearly. Show a minimal document, the intended meaning and the ambiguity or failure you observed. Distinguish a specification issue from a validator or site defect.

The repository is [github.com/gfrancodev/visualspec](https://github.com/gfrancodev/visualspec). Visual Spec is created and maintained by [Gustavo Franco](https://github.com/gfrancodev). Its current governance is maintainer-led and its 1.0 implementation is a release candidate.

## Choose the right path
- Fix spelling, links and explanatory examples with a focused pull request.
- Report defects with a minimal reproduction and the relevant version.
- Propose normative changes, new profiles or compatibility changes through an RFC.
- Contribute adapter evidence with an explicit capability list and reproducible tests.

Do not include private source documents, credentials or assets you cannot redistribute. Small synthetic examples are often better reproductions than complete production designs.

## Work locally
```sh
npm install
npm test
npm run build
```

For schema or validator changes, add a positive example and a negative case that fails for the intended reason. For site changes, check navigation, keyboard operation and narrow-screen layout. Update generated artifacts when their authoritative inputs change.

## What a review needs
Explain the problem, final behavior, compatibility impact and verification. Link the issue or RFC when applicable. A proposed behavior remains proposed until accepted and implemented; do not describe an unimplemented adapter as supported.

Read the repository's CONTRIBUTING.md and GOVERNANCE.md for the complete process.
